name: H&R Block, Inc.

profile.description: H&R Block, Inc. is a leading provider of tax preparation services, financial products, and small business solutions in the United States, Canada, and Australia. Founded in 1955 and headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, the company serves millions of clients annually through approximately 10,000 retail offices, digital DIY tax software, and AI-enhanced assisted tax preparation. New CEO Curtis Campbell succeeded Jeff Jones on January 1, 2026, inheriting a business transformed by the Block Horizons strategy, AI Tax Assist, and Upfront Transparent Pricing. The company employs approximately 3,000 year-round associates plus tens of thousands of seasonal tax professionals.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Under outgoing CEO Jeff Jones (2017-2025), H&R Block executed the Block Horizons strategic transformation that delivered a 123% stock price increase, introduced Upfront Transparent Pricing (eliminating the industry's most common client complaint), and launched AI Tax Assist [1][2]. These represent meaningful modernization of a 70-year-old business model, though the core service of tax preparation remains fundamentally unchanged. AI Deployment (1/2): AI Tax Assist is shipping to customers and actively used across the tax platform, with management citing broader use of artificial intelligence tools as a driver of Q3 FY2026 results [1]. However, no specific quantified revenue or cost savings attributable to AI have been disclosed. Market Share (1/2): H&R Block is the #2 tax preparation provider behind Intuit (TurboTax), with stable market share in both the assisted and DIY segments. Q3 FY2026 results showed improved client retention and stronger assisted category trends, suggesting share stabilization [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): The new CEO Curtis Campbell is expected to continue the digital transformation and AI integration strategy. The company's FY2026 outlook raise signals continued execution, though specific next-generation product announcements have not been made [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): H&R Block has invested meaningfully in technology and AI capabilities relative to its tax preparation peers, positioning itself ahead of traditional competitors in digital tax solutions.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): H&R Block's purpose centers on "providing help and inspiring confidence in our clients and communities everywhere," connecting the company's work to the broader goal of making tax filing and financial management accessible to all Americans [2]. This purpose is specific, thoughtful, and has been consistently executed since 1955, with the company's services disproportionately serving working-class and middle-income taxpayers who benefit most from professional tax assistance. Community Impact (1/2): H&R Block provides meaningful community impact through tax assistance programs for underserved communities and financial literacy initiatives. The company's service model inherently supports community financial wellbeing, though no specific foundation or dollar amounts for charitable programs were identified [2]. Employee Retention (2/2): Jones cited "record-high associate engagement" and the company's regular recognition on best places to work lists during his tenure [2]. H&R Block's transformation was featured in a 2024 Harvard Business School case study ("Driving Transformation - Jeff Jones at H&R Block"), suggesting the culture is recognized as distinctive. The "high-performing connected culture" described by management reflects genuine organizational health. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO transition period (Jones retiring, Campbell assuming leadership) makes insider buying patterns less meaningful. No evidence of significant net insider buying was identified in the past 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. H&R Block delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with revenue of \.4B (up 5.3% YoY), EBITDA of \.1B (up 5.9%), and adjusted EPS of \.02 (up 11.9%), leading management to raise the full-year FY2026 outlook to revenue of \.910-\.920B and adjusted EPS of \.10-\.20 [1][3]. The forward P/E of 6.5 is exceptional value territory, well below the 20 target. Profit margin of 18.9% approaches the 20% ideal. The payout ratio of 29.9% is well-managed, and the dividend has been paid consecutively since the company went public in 1962 — over 60 years of uninterrupted payments [3]. The key structural weakness is debt-to-equity of approximately 2,278%, which scores at the floor — this is driven by negative shareholders' equity resulting from \.0B+ of cumulative share repurchases that have reduced the equity base below zero [3]. ROE is technically undefined/negative with negative equity, also scoring at the floor. Despite these two zero-score items, the exceptional dividend history, low payout ratio, strong forward P/E, and near-target profit margin produce a solid infrastructure score [5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): H&R Block's core business faces meaningful AI substitution risk. AI-powered tax preparation tools — including those from competitors like Intuit and standalone AI assistants — can increasingly handle simple-to-moderate tax returns that represent a significant portion of DIY volume [1]. The assisted tax preparation segment is more defensible, as clients seeking human expertise for complex returns, audit protection, and fiduciary trust are less likely to rely on AI alone. However, as AI accuracy and confidence improve, the boundary between simple and complex returns will shift, gradually expanding the addressable market for AI-only solutions. H&R Block's regulatory moat is moderate — while tax preparation is regulated, it does not require the same licensing barriers as legal or medical professions. The company's physical retail network (approximately 10,000 offices) creates switching costs and brand trust but also represents fixed-cost exposure if client volumes shift to digital. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI Tax Assist is actively shipping to customers and integrated across the tax platform, with management citing AI tools as a contributor to Q3 FY2026 outperformance [1]. The company is proactively using AI to augment rather than replace its human tax professionals, positioning itself to benefit from AI adoption rather than be disrupted by it.

infinite_game.summary: H&R Block under Jeff Jones played a distinctly infinite game — the Block Horizons strategy invested in long-term transformation, the "high-performing connected culture" built organizational trust, and the company's 70-year commitment to helping people with taxes represents a durable purpose that has survived multiple leadership transitions and industry disruptions. The succession to Curtis Campbell appears smooth and aligned with the existing strategy. Sinek would appreciate the cultural investment and purpose-driven transformation but might question whether the company's aggressive capital return (\B+ in buybacks) prioritizes financial engineering over long-term capability building.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): H&R Block's purpose of helping people navigate taxes and finances has been consistently executed since 1955 — over 70 years spanning multiple leadership transitions, industry disruptions (from paper to software to AI), and competitive cycles [2]. The company's services disproportionately serve working-class and middle-income Americans, adding a social dimension to the commercial purpose. The Block Horizons strategy and AI Tax Assist investments demonstrate that purpose drives strategic decisions. However, the purpose — while genuine and enduring — is not so bold that it could never be fully achieved, distinguishing it from a truly transcendent Just Cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (2/2): H&R Block under Jones achieved "record-high associate engagement" and earned regular recognition on best places to work lists [2]. The transformation was featured in a 2024 Harvard Business School case study, and Jones specifically highlighted the "high-performing connected culture" as a key achievement of his tenure [2]. The smooth CEO succession from Jones to Campbell — with Jones remaining as Strategic Advisor through September 2026 — demonstrates organizational maturity and trust. The culture appears to be a genuine competitive advantage rather than a corporate talking point.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): H&R Block competes directly with Intuit/TurboTax, the dominant player in DIY tax preparation, and uses this competitive pressure to improve its own offerings rather than engage in zero-sum warfare. The development of AI Tax Assist and Upfront Transparent Pricing were direct responses to competitive dynamics — improving the H&R Block experience rather than merely attacking competitors' weaknesses [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): H&R Block has evolved meaningfully from a paper-based, office-only tax preparation company to a digital-hybrid model integrating AI, mobile filing, and transparent pricing. The Block Horizons strategy represented a significant modernization effort [2]. However, the core business model — preparing taxes for a fee — has remained fundamentally the same for 70 years. The company has adapted its delivery mechanism but has not made the kind of transformative pivot that defines existential flexibility (e.g., abandoning a core business to enter an entirely new market).

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Jones demonstrated courage in investing in the Block Horizons transformation and embracing AI when many traditional service companies were resistant. The decision to implement Upfront Transparent Pricing — eliminating surprise fees that were a short-term revenue lever — showed willingness to sacrifice near-term revenue for long-term client trust [2]. However, the aggressive \.0B+ capital return program (70% dividend increase plus 40% share reduction) reflects financial engineering that Sinek would view as prioritizing shareholder metrics over organizational reinvestment.

investment_thesis: H&R Block trades at a compelling 6.5x forward earnings with a 4.7% dividend yield supported by a conservative 29.9% payout ratio and 63 consecutive years of dividend payments [3][5]. Q3 FY2026 results demonstrated the durability of the franchise with 5.3% revenue growth, 11.9% EPS growth, and a raised full-year outlook to \.91-\.92B revenue and \.10-\.20 adjusted EPS [1]. The Block Horizons transformation under Jones created a modernized platform with AI Tax Assist, digital capabilities, and transparent pricing that positions the company well for the AI era. The smooth CEO succession to Curtis Campbell provides strategic continuity. With .8M in trailing net income and a proven capital return track record (\B+ returned under Jones), H&R Block offers a rare combination of deep value, reliable income, and modest growth.
thesis_continued: The primary risk is AI disruption of the tax preparation industry. As AI tools become increasingly capable of handling complex tax returns, the addressable market for human-assisted tax preparation could shrink over time. H&R Block's proactive AI integration (AI Tax Assist) mitigates but does not eliminate this risk [1]. The company's negative shareholders' equity (driven by \B+ in cumulative buybacks) creates an unusual balance sheet profile with \.03B in debt against effectively no equity cushion — while manageable at current interest rates and profitability levels, this leaves minimal margin for error during a downturn [5]. The CEO transition from Jones to Campbell introduces execution risk, though the smooth succession plan and Jones's advisory role through September 2026 provide continuity [2]. Revenue growth of 5.4% 5-year CAGR is modest, and the highly seasonal business model (Q3 fiscal year drives approximately 65% of annual revenue during tax season) creates uneven cash flow patterns.
key_catalysts: Continued AI Tax Assist adoption driving improved client retention, higher per-return revenue, and operational efficiency across the tax platform [1]
Forward P/E of 6.5x with PEG of 0.62 suggests significant upside potential if the market revalues HRB in line with its 11.9% EPS growth rate and 4.7% dividend yield
New CEO Curtis Campbell bringing fresh strategic perspective while maintaining the Block Horizons transformation momentum and record-high associate engagement culture [2]
key_risks: AI disruption of tax preparation could gradually shrink the addressable market for human-assisted returns, with AI tools from competitors and standalone assistants handling increasingly complex filings
Negative shareholders' equity from \B+ cumulative buybacks leaves no equity cushion — a severe downturn combined with \.03B debt could create liquidity pressure
CEO succession from Jones to Campbell introduces execution risk during a critical period of AI-driven industry transformation, with the new leader untested at scale [2]
